content:
Guiding Claude (Opus 5.5), a Lean4 proof of a polynomial time algorithm to
solve the Hamiltonian path problem in 2D solid grid graphs has been generated.

As far as I know, this was an open problem that is now solved. Umans and Lenhart solved the problem for Hamiltonian cycles in 2d solid grid graphs (1997) but I believe the problem of finding Hamiltonian paths in 2d solid grid graphs has remained open until now.

This problem has also been accepted to the Palomar Lean registry.

I've posted example code, a draft paper, description and the Lean4 code in a GitHub repository (SolidGridGraphHamPath) with the Lean proof located in the lean/ directory. The proof compiles with three axioms, propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

I have tried to do my due diligence to make sure the problem statement has been transferred over faithfully but if anyone finds flaws or other issues, I would welcome the feedback. I would also welcome any other constructive criticism about the project or proof.
This topic was moved here from #computer science > Polytime alg for Hamiltonian paths in 2d solid grid graphs by Michael Rothgang.
Wasn't this problem solved in 2002 by Umans and Lenhart? https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/646138
@Zzyv Zzyzek Your message was moved here by a moderator, please do not double post in the computer science channel.

Umans and Lenhart solved the Hamiltonian cycle problem in 2d solid grid graphs in 1997. The problem for Hamiltonian paths on 2d solid grid graphs has been open since then.

I've also posted a Lean formalization of Umans and Lenhart's algorithm (Zulip post, repo).
